習.meaning: A penguin signs up for night school. Every evening she dips two <part>feathers</part> in a pot of <part>white</part> paint and copies the teacher's letters onto the blackboard, wobble by wobble. By the end of term she can write her own name. She's starting to <kanji>learn</kanji>.
習.on: Her homework is to write the whole alphabet on the sole of a <sound>shoe</sound>.
習.kun: '<sound>Nah</sound>, try again,' says the teacher, so she practises until the whole class cheers '<sound>Rah</sound>!'

編.meaning: Overnight a spider takes down every note from the village <part>notice board</part>, lost cats, cake sales, a missing wig, and stitches them together with its own <part>thread</part>. In the morning a fat book hangs on the board: the whole year's <kanji>compilation</kanji>.
編.on: The first reader is a nosy <sound>hen</sound>, pecking through the pages for gossip.
編.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>!' clucks the hen, and asks the spider to knit her a scarf as well.

庁.meaning: On a quiet <part>street</part> stands a tiny garden <part>shed</part> with a brass plate on the door. Inside, one clerk stamps forms for the whole country: dog licences, rocket permits, moon parking. It's the national <kanji>agency</kanji> for everything.
庁.on: The clerk wears a tight lace <sound>cho</sound>ker that squeaks every time she brings the stamp down.
庁.kun: Out in the back <sound>ya</sound>rd, a <sound>cu</sound>ckoo runs a little <sound>sho</sound>p selling the blank forms.

損.meaning: An office <part>employee</part> uses a ship's <part>anchor</part> as a paperweight. When the fan starts blowing, he slams it down hard: it crashes through his desk, three floors and the boss's aquarium. The boss stands in the puddle and adds up the <kanji>damage</kanji>.
損.on: A soggy <sound>som</sound>brero floats up out of the broken aquarium.
損.kun: His <sound>so</sound>cks are soaked, so he hangs them to dry on a <sound>co</sound>t in the basement.

訳.meaning: A tailor holds his <part>measure</part> up against a foreign king's <part>speech</part>, snips it into pieces and stitches the words back together in a new language, each one cut to fit. At last the crowd understands. He knows how to <kanji>translate</kanji>.
訳.on: As thanks, the king hands him a spiky <sound>yuc</sound>ca plant in a gold pot.
訳.kun: '<sound>Wah</sound>!' wails the king's baby, who wants to know why the tailor brought <sound>ke</sound>tchup to a palace.

策.meaning: A panda wants the berries hidden inside a <part>thorn bush</part>. It lashes <part>bamboo</part> canes into a long grabber with a fork on the end, creeps up at midnight in a fake moustache and fishes them out one by one. It's a cunning <kanji>scheme</kanji>.
策.on: For dessert it sneaks into the garden centre and steals a fat <sound>suc</sound>culent too.

略.meaning: A painter is paid to paint <part>each</part> <part>rice field</part> in the valley, all two hundred of them. After three, she paints one big green square, writes 'etc.' underneath and goes for lunch. Nobody ever notices the <kanji>omission</kanji>.
略.on: Over lunch she sings an a<sound>ria</sound>, the 'ree-ah' squeezed into one quick note, and a <sound>cu</sound>ckoo joins in.
略.kun: She sips something <sound>ho</sound>t from a <sound>bo</sound>ttle and calls the job finished, or almost.

滅.meaning: A grumpy little <part>fire</part> builds a <part>barricade</part> of logs around itself and dares the world to come in. A cloud just shrugs and lets fall <part>water drops</part>, plink, plink, until logs and flames are a soggy black puddle. One cloud is enough to <kanji>destroy</kanji> it.
滅.on: The <sound>me</sound>ssy smoke drifts up the cloud's nose: '<sound>Tsu</sound>!'
滅.kun: All that's left is one <sound>ho</sound>t <sound>ro</sound>ck, hissing in the puddle.

遊.meaning: On a rainy day, a <part>child</part> turns the living room into a pirate ship: a bedsheet <part>sail</part>, an ironing board for a <part>diving board</part>, and a sofa cushion <part>ramp</part> down into a sea of pillows. Dad wanders in and is made to walk the plank. Time to <kanji>play</kanji>.
遊.on: The ship's mascot is a toy <sound>u</sound>nicorn, always first down the ramp.
遊.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>, a sea monster!' shouts the child, and throws a <sound>so</sound>ck at Dad.

条.meaning: A lawyer sits on a <part>folding chair</part> under a <part>tree</part>, writing the rules of the park: no juggling, no yodelling, no hugging squirrels. Each rule is nailed to the trunk with a big number on it. Every one is an <kanji>article</kanji>.
条.on: A little <sound>jo</sound>ey pops out of its mum's pouch and reads article one aloud.
条.kun: An <sound>e</sound>gg wobbles on a twig above his head, and a mother bird coos '<sound>Da</sound>rling, don't fall.'

象.meaning: A <part>pig</part> is tired of being small. It drapes a grey <part>wrap</part> over its back, stuffs a vacuum hose into its <part>mouth</part> for a trunk and tapes on just <part>one</part> floppy cabbage-leaf ear. At the zoo nobody blinks: it's an <kanji>elephant</kanji>, near enough.
象.on: Soon it has its own <sound>show</sound>, trumpeting through the hose twice a day.
象.kun: Then the zoo's <sound>ca</sound>rp, its <sound>ta</sound>co seller and its <sound>do</sound>ctor all dress up as elephants too, copying the pig.

印.meaning: A short postwoman tapes a rubber <part>stamp</part> to the end of a long <part>pole</part>, so she can reach the letterboxes on the twentieth floor. Thump, thump: every letter in the tower gets the same purple <kanji>stamp</kanji>, and so does one surprised window cleaner.
印.on: The purple comes from a whole bucket of <sound>in</sound>k slopped onto the pad.
印.kun: The window cleaner points at the purple mark on his bedding: '<sound>She</sound> <sound>ru</sound>ined my <sound>shee</sound>ts!'

厚.meaning: Under a <part>cliff</part>, a <part>child</part> is so worried about the <part>sun</part> that she puts on twelve coats, five scarves and a duvet. She looks like a walking mattress and can't bend her arms. Her layers are very <kanji>thick</kanji>.
厚.on: She still manages to lick an ice cream <sound>co</sound>ne through a gap in the scarves.
厚.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>... <sound>tsu</sound>!' she sneezes, but under all that wool nobody hears a thing.

塁.meaning: On a frozen <part>rice field</part>, kids pile up <part>soil</part> and blocks of <part>ice</part> into little walls at all four corners. Each crew guards its own corner with a stack of snowballs and a very stern face. The field now has four <kanji>bases</kanji>.
塁.on: When spring comes, the ice melts and each fort sags into a muddy <sound>ru</sound>in.
塁.kun: On <sound>to</sound>p of the biggest fort, a <sound>ree</sound>d flag flutters over a <sound>de</sound>ckchair throne.

縮.meaning: The owner of a tiny <part>inn</part> pulls one loose <part>thread</part> on the curtains, and the whole building puckers like a sock in hot water: rooms squeeze together, beds fold up, guests pop out of the windows. The inn begins to <kanji>shrink</kanji>.
縮.on: By the end it's no bigger than a <sound>su</sound>gar <sound>cu</sound>be.
縮.kun: The guests sit outside eating <sound>chee</sound>se on the roof of a <sound>jee</sound>p, waiting for it to stretch back.

介.meaning: A packed bus stop, one <part>umbrella</part>, and two strangers under it leaning apart like a <part>slash</part> and a <part>pole</part>. A third, soaking wet, wriggles in between them until nobody can lift an arm. He's well and truly <kanji>jammed in</kanji>.
介.on: Then a gust tears the umbrella free and it soars away like a <sound>ki</sound>te.

舞.meaning: At midnight a scarecrow with <part>mismatched legs</part> hops off its post, plops an <part>empty basket</part> on its head and lurches round the field: long leg, short leg, long leg, spin. The crows love it and copy every move. It's a brand new <kanji>dance</kanji>.
舞.on: The farmer chases them on a <sound>bu</sound>lldozer, but soon the bulldozer is swaying too.
舞.kun: '<sound>Ma</sound>, look, it's dancing!' squawks a baby crow from the fence.

汚.meaning: A mud wrestler gets home and squeezes into a tiny tub of <part>water drops</part> with <part>two</part> muddy boots still on, scrubbing with his towel <part>wrap</part>. In a minute the water's brown, the towel's brown, the cat's brown. Everything is <kanji>dirty</kanji>.
汚.on: An <sound>o</sound>ctopus climbs up out of the drain, takes one look and climbs straight back down.
汚.kun: Then he drops a pot of <sound>yo</sound>gurt on his swimming <sound>go</sound>ggles too.

染.meaning: A florist wants a rainbow <part>tree</part>. She hires <part>nine</part> cats to carry buckets of coloured <part>water drops</part> up the trunk and tip them over the leaves: red, green, purple. By sunset the cats are purple too. Everything has soaked up the <kanji>dye</kanji>.
染.on: The park's <sound>sen</sound>try stares down at his boots, now bright orange.
染.kun: Even the gardener's <sound>so</sound>cks come out with purple stripes.

展.meaning: A magician pulls a tiny <part>flag</part> on a <part>pole</part> out of his hat. He tugs, and it opens into <part>two</part> flags, then a tablecloth, a <part>garment</part>, a parachute, a circus tent. It just won't stop: watch it <kanji>unfold</kanji>.
展.on: Out of the tent steps a <sound>ten</sound>or, already halfway through his song.

属.meaning: A stray <part>lizard</part> keeps sneaking onto the same ship. One day the captain paints the ship's <part>flag</part> on its back, gives it a bowl, a bunk and a tiny hat. At last it has somewhere to <kanji>belong</kanji>.
属.on: On costume night it dresses as a <sound>zo</sound>mbie and hides in the captain's <sound>cu</sound>ckoo clock.
属.kun: Promoted, it now runs the ship's <sound>sa</sound>rdine <sound>carn</sound>ival: a junior official.

暗.meaning: The town's <part>chime</part> is so loud that when it strikes noon, the <part>sun</part> jumps and hides behind a hill. Streetlights flicker on, owls wake up, people walk into lampposts. In the middle of the day, the town sinks into <kanji>darkness</kanji>.
暗.on: Your <sound>un</sound>cle stumbles about with a candle, calling for the sun to come back.
暗.kun: In the gloom a <sound>cu</sound>ckoo pops out of its clock and shouts '<sound>Rah</sound>!' at nobody.

境.meaning: A <part>bellhop</part> walks round the hotel garden dragging his heel through the <part>soil</part>, drawing a line: guests on this side, goats on that. Step over it and you get a stern little cough. That line is the <kanji>boundary</kanji>.
境.on: A goat steps over with a room <sound>key</sound> in its mouth, and the bellhop squeaks '<sound>Oh</sound>!' so fast that the two run together.
境.kun: He repaints the line with <sound>sa</sound>rdine oil from a <sound>ca</sound>rt, using a wriggling <sound>ee</sound>l as a brush.

求.meaning: A cactus in a pot holds up <part>one</part> spiky arm and points at a single <part>dot</part> on the map: the only <part>water</part> for miles. Then it writes the gardener a polite note: 'Please, just a splash.' It's a formal <kanji>request</kanji>.
求.on: The gardener chalks a pool <sound>cue</sound> and taps the watering can over toward the pot.
求.kun: The cactus also asks for a <sound>mo</sound>p to be left on <sound>to</sound>p of the shelf, for the spills.

及.meaning: A sleepy cat spots a <part>pretzel</part> on the far end of the counter. Without getting up, its paw shoots out in one long <part>slash</part>, longer than any cat's paw should be, stretching, stretching. Sometimes you just have to <kanji>reach out</kanji>.
及.on: When it still falls short, it nudges the pretzel closer with a pool <sound>cue</sound>.
及.kun: An <sound>o</sound>tter on the floor holds up a pot of <sound>yo</sound>gurt, and the paw reaches that too.

級.meaning: At knitting school, pupils are graded by the <part>catch net</part> they can knit from one <part>thread</part>. Beginners' nets catch flies, middle nets catch fish, the top nets catch whales. Each pupil wears a ribbon for the size of their net: that's their <kanji>class</kanji>.
級.on: The best knitter of all gets a golden pool <sound>cue</sound>, for reasons nobody remembers.

輪.meaning: A mobile <part>library</part> is bumping along in an old <part>car</part> when a tyre flies off. The librarian rolls up a giant scroll into a hoop, bolts it on, and off they go, the story turning as they ride. It's the world's first paper <kanji>wheel</kanji>.
輪.on: Its hub is a gold <sound>rin</sound>g that flashes in the sun with every turn.
輪.kun: '<sound>Wah</sound>!' shout the kids at the bus stop as the paper wheel spins past.

皇.meaning: On a snowy hill, the kids crown a snowman <part>king</part> and sit him on a sledge throne, <part>white</part> from crown to toes. By evening every snowman in town has turned to bow to him. He rules them all: the <kanji>emperor</kanji> of winter.
皇.on: His crown is an upside-down ice cream <sound>co</sound>ne with a cherry on the tip.

整.meaning: A squirrel ties her nuts into a neat <part>bundle</part>, flaps the dust away with a little paper <part>fan</part>, and checks every label is <part>correct</part> before she stacks it in her hollow. Rows by size, labels facing out. She loves to <kanji>organize</kanji>.
整.on: The very best nuts go in a tiny steel <sound>sa</sound>fe at the back.
整.kun: She hops from <sound>to</sound>p shelf to <sound>to</sound>p shelf, squeaking '<sound>No</sound>t neat yet!'

継.meaning: Grandma's will says only: 'Pull the <part>thread</part>.' You find it tied to a <part>pole</part> in her barn, give it a tug, and a trapdoor drops a mountain of <part>rice</part> on your head, plus her secret recipe book. It's all yours to <kanji>inherit</kanji>.
継.on: Recipe number one is her famous rice <sound>ca</sound>ke.
継.kun: '<sound>Tsu</sound>!' you sneeze in the rice dust, then take up the family cooking for <sound>goo</sound>d.
